The registry @8ff31fa1c8 and the boundary declarations @9c1a45ad28 are commit-pinned. The row names the class it answers: the wave-1 row schema's own provenance defect (@e4301b85f7 -> @587a4e18f7), where a v2 enum sat beside a provenance claiming v1.

surprises: TWO INDEPENDENT FIRM PARSES DIFFERED BY ONE ENTITY, AND THE RULING THAT FORBADE THE SECOND PARSE IS VINDICATED BY MY OWN DATA. Before 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X 80564 landed I had already measured this view's firm baseline with my own word-boundary parse: 1,819 measured entities, mdpf 26, cross-firm mean 0.433747. The SHARED cohort published by 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~X gives 1,820, mdpf 27, cross-firm mean 0.432832 over the same view. ONE ENTITY. The ruling's stated reason -- a second parse could differ by one token and the comparison would then be two cohorts -- is not a cautionary framing, it is what happened, and it would have made PRD sec 6.3 a comparison of unlike things while every number on both sides looked correct. The delivered row consumes the shared cohort; the self-parse is recorded as superseded.

THE 540's PER-MEMBER IDENTITIES ARE NOT DERIVABLE FROM THIS FACE'S PINNED SOURCES, and the honest consequence is an UNMEASURED disposition rather than a substituted number. The PRD's cohort rests on a census of 1,255 C3System nodes and 4,857 members-with-a-system; the store this face pins carries 4 C3System nodes and the AB materialize store carries 3. I can derive 14 members spanning both motif catalogues, or 614 with more than one family in-population -- neither IS the 540, and either one wearing the cohort's name would be a different quantity passing as the declared one. Routed as an observation: if the wave-2 fusion is expected to state a per-member disposition, the cohort's member list needs a pinned carrier that this face does not name.

THE VIEW THIS FACE PREPARES IS 78.7 PERCENT ABSENT OVER THE RATIFIED POPULATION (15,335 of 19,482), and that is worth stating loudly BEFORE the fusion consumes it: motif membership is declared for a minority of the cloud population, so the fused result's coverage will be dominated by view 1 wherever view 2 is ABSENT. This is exactly why ABSENT must not collapse to 0 -- a 0 would assert measured low affinity across four-fifths of the population, and the fusion would return a full matrix either way.

THE FIRM SEPARATION ON THIS VIEW IS SMALL: +0.033638 on the SHARED cohort (within 0.466470 over 805,717 pairs vs cross 0.432832 over 849,573; pair frame 1,655,290 = C(1820,2)). Reported as measured and NOT interpreted here, because 6.3's threshold is the design lane's. Recorded because a reader meeting the PRD's 0.989 / 0.974 alongside it could take this for a regression, and it is not the same measurement -- different views, different population, different denominator. For scale, view 1 reports 0.167169 with ratio 6.429 over the same cohort; the difference is a fact about the two views, not a verdict on either. FOUND BY MY OWN RESIDUAL SWEEP, NOT BY THE CERTIFIER: this entry previously carried the SUPERSEDED self-parse figures (0.032738 / 805,691 / 847,780) as though they were the measurement. The certifier named THREE proof carriers to repair (AC9, commit_or_etag, spec_ref); this was a FOURTH, and it was asserting a count rather than describing the divergence -- the distinction that decides whether a superseded number may stay. A NAMED DEFECT IS A SAMPLE, NOT A CENSUS, applied forward for the second time in this session: the sweep must cover every carrier of a number, not the ones a reviewer happened to open.

INSTRUMENT NOTE ON THE ALIGNMENT: 68 of the view's 4,215 members do not appear in the ratified population and are carried ABSENT. They are neither dropped nor evidence of a defect on either side -- the population is edge-incident-and-non-semctl by its own definition, so a member outside it is expected. Naming the number rather than silently intersecting is what keeps the fusion over the UNION.
